newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia guerrillas respond to Samper statement.
newsitem.headline: Colombia guerrillas respond to Samper statement.

text.p: With the release of 60 Colombian soldiers at stake, President Ernesto Samper warned his army on Monday that undercover operations were forbidden in a zone demilitarized as part of a deal with their guerrilla captors.
In a response issued on Monday night, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia praised Samper's action.

"We welcome the decision taken by the Supreme Commander of the Colombian Armed Forces (the president) and this will undoubtedly be an important step in winning the prompt release of the prisoners," said a communique issued to reporters.

The guerrillas sent a letter to government negotiators and Catholic Church representatives inviting them to a meeting near the jungle town of Remolinos del Caguan on Tuesday morning to finalise the terms for the handover of the captive troops.

Samper's comments come less than 24 hours after leftist rebels said undercover military operations in the jungles of Caqueta province could hamper the release of the troops, held for more than nine months.

Samper ordered government troops to pull out of a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) area of Caqueta to allow rebels to release the 60 soldiers, captured in an attack in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30.

Late Sunday, FARC commanders issued a communique saying some of the 5,000 troops withdrawn from the neutral zone returned, posing as street vendors. Gen. Agustin Ardila, commander of the army's Fourth Division, rejected the claim.
